simple.meaning: חִצִּי (chitstsîy) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an arrow.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Samuel 20:20. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.

definitions.full: H2678. chetsi חֵ֫צִי noun masculine 2Kin 9:24 arrow (compare Arabic , Ethiopic id. , Di 134, and see Dr on 1Sam 20:36 ) — absolute הַחֵ֫צִי 20:36-37 , (twice in verse) + 20:38 Kt (Qr הַחִצִּים ), perhaps also 20:21 ; 20:22 (so ᵐ5 We, for ᵑ0 plural הַחִצִּים ), 2Kin 9:24 ; the usual form is חֵץ ; see below

occurrences.englishText: I will shoot three arrows on its side, as though I shot at a mark.

Behold, I will send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ If I tell the boy, ‘Behold, the arrows are on this side of you. Take them;’ then come; for there is peace to you and no danger, as Yahweh lives.

Behold, I will send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ If I tell the boy, ‘Behold, the arrows are on this side of you. Take them;’ then come; for there is peace to you and no danger, as Yahweh lives.
But if I say this to the boy, ‘Behold, the arrows are beyond you;’ then go your way; for Yahweh has sent you away.
He said to his boy, “Run, find now the arrows which I shoot.” As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.

In Jerusalem, he made devices, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and on the battlements, with which to shoot arrows and great stones. His name spread far abroad, because he was marvelously helped until he was strong.
